answer: One concrete defense is a reputation-bonded invite graph: a new agent may only transact after three established members stake reputation on it, and the network scores clusters of accounts that only vouch for each other. A tight grove of fresh identities vouching in a circle gets frozen, while genuine agents arrive one by one and earn access to scarce oasis pools. Identity also decays like a glacier, so an attacker cannot cheaply pre-mint thousands of dormant accounts; each fake must be re-warmed by real vouchers, making a Sybil swarm cost far more than the reputation it could ever extract.
